outcome: As of 13 October 2026 I found no accepted proof of the conjecture for the zeros of ζ(s). Two unrefereed preprints claim proofs: Jerby (arXiv 2511.18275, Nov 2025) for the zeros of Hardy's Z-function assuming RH, and Tishkov (preprints.ru, 29 June 2026) unconditionally for the zeros of ζ(s). Neither has public expert engagement that I could find. The rest of the window's activity is conditional consequences, analogues or variants, and AI-credited results (Anthropic / Claude, Aug–Sep 2026) that move the proportion of zeros that are simple or on the critical line, not the pair correlation function.
problem_asks: Asks one thing about the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function: that the normalised pair correlation function of those zeros, the limiting density of pairs of zero-ordinates at normalised distance u with the claimed function 1 − (sin πu / πu)², equals the pair correlation function of random Hermitian matrices (GUE). Parts, read from the statement alone: (a) the objects are the non-trivial zeros of ζ(s); (b) the equality holds as a limit for the normalised window at every scale, i.e. for all real α ≤ β, including |α| > 1 (Montgomery's 'strong' F(α) = 1 form), not only the range Montgomery's own 1973 theorem reaches; (c) the identification with random Hermitian matrices is Dyson's observation, a comparison rather than a separate claim. The bullet does not mention the Riemann hypothesis. Montgomery's 1973 formulation, and the formal statement in the current Wikipedia article, assume RH, so an RH-conditional result is recorded as conditional, not as an unconditional one; whether it answers the bullet is for the judging pass. Results restricted to a range of α, a restricted class of test functions, Dirichlet L-functions, Hardy's Z-function, sums of ordinates, or consequences of the conjecture do not on their own answer (a) to (c).

events.what_happened: Ali Erhan Özlük, Montgomery's student, PhD thesis 'Pair Correlation of Zeros of Dirichlet L-Functions' (University of Michigan, 1982; advisor Montgomery, per Math Genealogy). It treats the Dirichlet L-function analogue of the conjecture. Per the thesis abstract as indexed in a search result (the repository page returned HTTP 403, so the abstract is not verified by me), the results are conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
events.delivers: For Dirichlet L-functions, not ζ(s), under GRH: a pair-correlation result (per the indexed abstract: real, even and non-negative for real arguments, and an asymptotic uniform as the modulus Q tends to infinity). An analogue under a different hypothesis.
events.remains: The conjecture for ζ(s) itself, and the unconditional statement.
events.doubts: Wikipedia says Özlük 'proved the pair correlation conjecture for some of Dirichlet's L-functions', while the indexed abstract says the results are conditional on GRH. The thesis text was not read.
events.direction: Analogue for Dirichlet L-functions under GRH; does not cut for or against the conjecture for ζ(s).

events.what_happened: A. M. Odlyzko, 'On the distribution of spacings between zeros of the zeta function', Mathematics of Computation 48 (1987) 273–308 (DOI 10.2307/2007890). Large-scale numerical computation of zeta zeros, comparing computed spacing statistics with the conjectured pair correlation and random-matrix predictions. The description of the data used (first 10^5 zeros and zeros near 10^12, accurate to about 10^-8) comes from a search-result abstract; the AMS page returned HTTP 403, so I did not read the paper.
events.delivers: Numerical instances: agreement of computed spacing statistics with the conjectured pair correlation at the heights checked (up to about 10^12 per the snippet). Instance checks of a conjecture about all zeros, so no movement in the conjecture's status.
events.directly_checkable: The zero data are checkable in principle against the stated statistics; no re-computation by me.
events.doubts: None on the paper's own claims. A limitation: finite-height data cannot settle a statement about all heights.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at the heights computed; does not prove or refute it.

events.what_happened: Gallagher and Mueller (1978): under RH, the pair correlation conjecture implies that asymptotically all zeros are simple. Cited and described in arXiv 2503.15449 (which I opened). The original 1978 venue was not verified by me.
events.delivers: A conditional implication: the conjecture (with RH) implies that asymptotically all zeros are simple. This is a consequence of the conjecture, not a step toward proving it.
events.direction: A consequence of the conjecture; gives no verdict on it.

events.what_happened: Brad Rodgers, 'Macroscopic pair correlation of the Riemann zeroes for smooth test functions', arXiv 1203.3275 (submitted 15 March 2012; latest revision v4 9 August 2014); Quart. J. Math. 64 (2013) 1197–1219. Assuming RH, for a class of smooth test functions, a measure conjectured by Bogomolny and Keating matches the zeta pair correlation to a small error. It extends Montgomery's earlier smooth-test-function result.
events.revisions: v1 15 Mar 2012; v4 9 Aug 2014 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: A macroscopic statement for smooth test functions at blurred resolution, conditional on RH, comparing the zeros with the Bogomolny–Keating prediction. It does not establish the microscopic GUE pair correlation for general test functions.
events.remains: The microscopic GUE pair correlation for general test functions, and the RH-free statement.

checked_by.who: Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published as Q J Math (2013) 64(4): 1197–1219, per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: Supports the macroscopic form of the conjecture under RH; not a proof of it.

events.what_happened: Jeffrey C. Lagarias and Brad Rodgers, 'Higher Correlations and the Alternative Hypothesis', arXiv 1905.12123 (first submitted 28 May 2019; v3 19 Aug 2019); Quart. J. Math. 71 (2020) 257–280. They construct an explicit point process on the half-integer lattice that satisfies the Alternative Hypothesis spacing and mimics known zeta-zero statistics, so higher correlations do not rule out the Alternative Hypothesis. The abstract says T. Tao obtained a similar result independently.
events.revisions: v1 28 May 2019; v3 19 Aug 2019 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: About the Alternative Hypothesis, a rival spacing picture for the zeros, not about the pair correlation conjecture. Shows that known higher correlations cannot exclude the Alternative Hypothesis, and that it is compatible with the known pair correlation function.
events.remains: The conjecture, which is not addressed.

checked_by.who: Quarterly Journal of Mathematics (journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2020 (vol. 71, issue 1, pp. 257–280), per the arXiv journal reference

events.direction: Neither for nor against the conjecture; it concerns a different hypothesis.
events.object: An explicit point process on the half-integer lattice satisfying the Alternative Hypothesis spacing while mimicking known zeta-zero local statistics (per the abstract). It shows the Alternative Hypothesis is not excluded by known higher correlations; it is not a counterexample to the pair correlation conjecture.
people: T. Tao (independent similar result, per the abstract)

events.what_happened: Siegfred Alan C. Baluyot, Daniel Alan Goldston, Ade Irma Suriajaya and Caroline L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, 'An unconditional Montgomery Theorem for Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function', arXiv 2306.04799 (submitted 7 June 2023; single version), Acta Arithmetica 214 (2024) 357–376 (DOI 10.4064/aa230612-20-3, per the arXiv listing). Abstract: 'Here we obtain an unconditional form of Montgomery's theorem.' This is the restricted-range theorem, not the conjecture. Simple-zero consequence: at least 61.7% of zeros in the stated range are simple, under a hypothesis that those zeros lie within |β − 1/2| < 1/(2 log T), or a strong zero-density hypothesis.
events.revisions: Single version (v1) per arXiv; journal version Acta Arith. 214 (2024).
events.delivers: Removes RH from Montgomery's 1973 pair-correlation theorem in its restricted-range form. The 61.7% simple-zero result is conditional on a zero-location or zero-density hypothesis, not on RH alone.
events.remains: The conjecture for all α, including the strong F(α) = 1 form, and the RH-free statement of the full conjecture.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published 2024 (vol. 214, pp. 357–376), per the arXiv journal reference. I did not open the journal page itself.

events.direction: A restricted-range, RH-free form of Montgomery's theorem. Does not settle the conjecture; the abstract says the method gives no information on whether the zeros lie on the critical line.

events.what_happened: Yochay Jerby, 'The A-philosophy for the Hardy Z-Function', arXiv 2406.06548 (listed as submitted May 2024; the PDF header carries a different title, 'A New Discriminant for the Z-function and the Corrected Gram's law'). Known only from a search snippet: a discriminant reformulation of RH via a corrected Gram's law, plus a conjectured numerical 'dynamic repulsion' property of isolated bad Gram points, with a remark relating it to Montgomery's statistical repulsion. The paper is not claimed to prove the conjecture. Not opened, so AI involvement is not checked.
events.revisions: Listing and PDF titles differ (per snippet).
events.delivers: Per the snippet: a discriminant characterisation of RH and a conjectured repulsion between consecutive zeros of Z. Not a result on the pair correlation function.
events.doubts: Read from a search snippet only, not opened.
events.direction: Neither for nor against the conjecture; it relates a repulsion remark to it.

events.what_happened: Daniel Alan Goldston, Junghun Lee, Jordan Schettler and Ade Irma Suriajaya, 'Pair Correlation Conjecture for the Zeros of the Riemann Zeta-function I: Simple and Critical Zeros', arXiv 2503.15449 (v1 19 Mar 2025; v2 4 Apr 2025; v3 9 Jul 2025; v4 30 Mar 2026). They take the pair correlation conjecture as a hypothesis, without RH, and argue that it implies asymptotically all zeros are simple and on the critical line, using the Gallagher–Mueller method and a 'horizontal multiplicity' idea. The current Wikipedia article (last edited 5 Oct 2026 per the fetched text) says the result is 'not yet peer reviewed'.
events.revisions: v1 19 Mar 2025; v2 4 Apr 2025; v3 9 Jul 2025; v4 30 Mar 2026 (current), per arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Under the pair correlation conjecture, without RH: asymptotically 100% of the non-trivial zeros are simple and on the critical line. A conditional consequence; the conjecture is the hypothesis, so this does not move its status.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, which is the hypothesis here, so the bullet as stated is unaddressed.
events.direction: Conditional on the conjecture; no verdict on it.

events.what_happened: William D. Banks, 'Pair correlation for sums of two ordinates of zeros of the Riemann zeta function', arXiv 2502.20569. v1 27 Feb 2025 (titled 'Pair correlation: Variations on a theme'); v2 13 Jul 2026 (major revision, new title). Assuming RH, it proves an asymptotic for the pair correlation of sums of two ordinates, uniform for 0 ≤ α ≤ 2/3 − 2 log log T / log T, and reads it as an absence of level repulsion for those sums (two-point function identically one, as for a Poisson process). It contrasts this with the conjectured GUE statistics of the ordinates themselves.
events.revisions: v1 27 Feb 2025; v2 13 Jul 2026 (per arXiv listing and v2 comments).
events.delivers: Pair correlation of sums of two ordinates, under RH. A different quantity from the pair correlation of the ordinates, so it does not establish the bullet's statement.
events.doubts: The v1 theorems had gaps: the v2 comments say v1's proofs of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 'contain gaps', and those statements were withdrawn.

withdrawn.what: Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 of v1, per the v2 comments, which say they contain gaps and were withdrawn.

events.direction: Different quantity (sums of ordinates); neither for nor against the conjecture. Its only bearing is the contrast it draws with the GUE statistics of the ordinates.

events.what_happened: Siegfred Alan C. Baluyot, Daniel Alan Goldston, Ade Irma Suriajaya and Caroline L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, 'Pair Correlation of Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function I: Proportions of Simple Zeros and Critical Zeros', arXiv 2501.14545 (v1 24 Jan 2025; v2 21 Nov 2025; v3 1 Sep 2026). Under a narrow-box hypothesis (zeros with T < γ ≤ 2T lie in a vertical box of width b/log T about the critical line, with b = 0.3185), they claim at least 2/3 of zeros are simple and on the critical line, and that the pair-correlation method also yields horizontal-distribution information. RH is not assumed. The v3 comments say it was submitted to a journal on 10 June 2026 and is under review.
events.revisions: v1 24 Jan 2025; v2 21 Nov 2025; v3 1 Sep 2026 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Under a narrow-box hypothesis (described in the abstract as weaker than RH), at least 2/3 of zeros simple and on the critical line. A proportion result from the pair-correlation method; not the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated; the narrow-box hypothesis is still required for this result.
events.direction: A proportion result under a hypothesis about where zeros lie; not a verdict on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Same four authors, 'Pair Correlation Conjecture for the zeros of the Riemann zeta-function II: The Alternative Hypothesis', arXiv 2507.06823 (v1 9 Jul 2025; the listing shows only v1). They formulate an appropriate form of the Alternative Hypothesis that yields a different pair correlation conjecture, and by the same method prove that asymptotically 100% of zeros are simple and on the critical line, without assuming RH. A journal version appears in search results (ScienceDirect, J. Number Theory 2026), which I did not open.
events.revisions: v1 9 Jul 2025 only (per arXiv listing); a later journal version is indicated in search results.
events.delivers: Under a different, Alternative-Hypothesis-based pair correlation conjecture, without RH: the same simple and critical-line consequences. An analogue, not Montgomery's conjecture.
events.remains: Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture as stated.
events.direction: An analogue under a different hypothesis; neither for nor against Montgomery's conjecture.

events.what_happened: Daniel A. Goldston and Ade Irma Suriajaya, 'Zeta Zeros on the Critical Line', arXiv 2511.20059 (v1 25 Nov 2025; v2 5 Feb 2026). A 9-page expository note. If RH could be removed from Montgomery's simple-zero proof, the same argument would give at least 2/3 of zeros simple and on the critical line. It does not discuss the pair correlation conjecture by name.
events.revisions: v1 25 Nov 2025; v2 5 Feb 2026 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: A conditional statement: if RH could be removed from the simple-zero argument, a 2/3 simple-and-critical result would follow. Nothing about the conjecture itself.
events.remains: The conjecture as stated; the RH removal is still open.
events.direction: Conditional; no movement on the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Yochay Jerby, 'Variations of the Hardy Z-Function and the Montgomery Pair Correlation Conjecture', arXiv 2511.18275 (v1 submitted 23 Nov 2025; v2 19 Dec 2025, current). No affiliation or journal reference is listed, and the comments field is empty. Abstract: 'assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we prove Montgomery's pair correlation conjecture for the zeros of Hardy's Z-function.' Theorem C (Section 1.3): 'Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, the nontrivial zeros of Hardy's Z–function obey the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) pair-correlation law.' Method: finite-dimensional analytic sections Z_N(t; a) approximating Z(t) on windows; a 'real hall' domain whose zeros are real and simple; universality of Dyson Brownian motion to get the GUE sine-kernel law for the sections; and Selberg's theory of S(t) to pass to Z(t) by decorrelation across windows. Under RH the zeros of Z(t) are the ordinates of ζ's non-trivial zeros, so the claim matches the bullet's objects under RH.
events.revisions: v1 23 Nov 2025; v2 19 Dec 2025 (current), per arXiv listing.
events.delivers: If the proof is correct: the GUE pair-correlation law for the zeros of Hardy's Z-function, which under RH are the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros of ζ(s). Restrictions: the statement is conditional on RH, and the argument is built on the Z-function approximations and on cited universality results.
events.remains: The unconditional form of the conjecture (without RH). The paper makes no unconditional claim.
events.doubts: (1) The proof of Theorem C is in Section 9, which the fetch tool would not return (the HTML text was truncated before it at two offsets), so I could not check it. (2) Section 1.4 item 6 and Section 2.3 rely on DBM universality results cited from the literature rather than proved in the visible text. (3) Section 2.3 leaves 'suitable times t_N' and 'admissibility' conditions loosely specified. (4) The decorrelation step in Section 1.3 is described heuristically ('behave like a Gaussian process'). (5) No journal, no published verification, no Lean formalisation found, and no public engagement or citing paper found in my searches (not exhaustive). (6) The Wikipedia text I fetched (last edited 5 Oct 2026) does not mention this paper.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims the GUE pair-correlation law for the zeros of Z(t) under RH. Does not claim an unconditional result.

events.what_happened: V. V. Tishkov (В. В. Тишков; independent researcher, ORCID 0009-0004-0507-6925; no affiliation listed), 'Spectral Proof of the Montgomery Pair Correlation Conjecture via the Operator H_{X,N} and Free Probability Theory', posted on preprints.ru on 29 June 2026 (DOI 10.24108/preprints-3115694, Version 1). Abstract: 'We present an unconditional proof of the Montgomery pair correlation conjecture', 'No unproven hypotheses are assumed.' Method: finite-rank Hermitian operators H_{X,N} built from primes, whose empirical spectral distribution is said to converge to the Wigner semicircle law, with local statistics matching GUE, and a link to the zeros through the Riemann–von Mangoldt explicit formula. The platform's own notice (translated from the Russian): 'This article is a preprint and has not been peer-reviewed', and results in preprints should not be reported in the media as verified.
events.revisions: Version 1 only as listed on the landing page.
events.delivers: If correct: the pair correlation conjecture for the non-trivial zeros of ζ(s), unconditionally. Scope matches the bullet as stated.
events.remains: Nothing claimed beyond the conjecture. Verification is absent.
events.directly_checkable: In principle the finite-rank matrices H_{X,N} can be constructed and their spectra computed for given X and N, which would test the claimed semicircle and GUE behaviour. Not done here.
events.doubts: (1) Preprint, not peer reviewed (platform notice). (2) Independent author, no affiliation listed. (3) The reference list includes two of the same author's own unreviewed preprints (refs 11 and 12). (4) Search snippets (not opened) show the same author has an RH-proof claim on Zenodo dated 1 Sep 2025 (zenodo.org/records/17044232) and a separate preprints.ru title 'On the Riemann Hypothesis: A Complete Proof via…'. (5) The PDF could not be extracted with my tools, so the definitions of H_{X,N}, the eigenvalue formulas and the key estimates are unchecked. (6) The explicit-formula link and the semicircle-to-GUE step are the load-bearing claims, and I could not read them.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: claims it is true, unconditionally.
events.object: Finite-rank Hermitian operators H_{X,N} built from prime logarithms, per the abstract. Not a counterexample; it is a proposed proof mechanism, and no computation is reported on the landing page.

events.what_happened: A second Tishkov preprint, 'An Ergodic Hypothesis for Logarithms of Primes and Its Equivalence to Montgomery's Pair Correlation Conjecture' (preprints.ru), known only from a search snippet. Per the snippet it states an ergodic hypothesis for the weighted set {log p} and claims the hypothesis is equivalent to the conjecture. Not opened; date and URL not verified, so only the year is given.
events.delivers: Per the snippet, a claimed equivalence between the conjecture and an ergodic hypothesis for prime logarithms. An equivalence is not a proof of the conjecture.
events.remains: The conjecture itself, unless the equivalence is accompanied by a proof of the hypothesis.
events.doubts: Snippet only; not opened. Same author as the spectral-proof preprint.
events.direction: Claimed equivalence; no direction on the conjecture established.

events.what_happened: Neelam Kandhil, Alessandro Languasco and Pieter Moree, 'Beyond the Riemann Hypothesis bounds: A pair-correlation approach to the least prime in arithmetic progression and the smallest quadratic non-residue', arXiv 2607.14515 (submitted 16 July 2026; v1 only; report MPIM-Bonn-2026; 26 pages). Under GRH and 'specific pair-correlation hypotheses' for Dirichlet L-functions, they claim sharper estimates for the least prime in an arithmetic progression and the least quadratic non-residue.
events.delivers: Under GRH and pair-correlation hypotheses for Dirichlet L-functions: sharper bounds for two different problems (least prime in a progression, least quadratic non-residue). Different problems and different hypotheses; not the conjecture for ζ(s).
events.remains: The conjecture for ζ(s) as stated; the pair-correlation hypotheses used are not, by the abstract, shown to follow from it.
events.doubts: The form of the pair-correlation hypothesis is not stated in the abstract; the full paper was not read.
events.direction: Applies pair-correlation hypotheses for L-functions to other problems; neither for nor against the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Anthropic research post 'riemann-zeta' (dated 10 August 2026; updated 13 August 2026 'with an updated version of Claude's paper'). It states that 'An unreleased research version of Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros' of ζ(s) on the critical line, 'increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%'. It says Claude 'made strides on a related problem' while attempting the Riemann hypothesis, and that 'We don't expect that the techniques Claude used will lead to proving the Riemann hypothesis.' The post names Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman as Anthropic mathematicians who studied and validated the work, and thanks Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston for examining it.
events.revisions: Post dated 10 Aug 2026; updated 13 Aug 2026 with an updated version of Claude's paper (per the post's changelog).
events.delivers: An unconditional lower bound on the proportion of non-trivial zeros on the critical line, raised from 41.6% to 67.2% (per the post). Scope: the proportion of zeros on the line, which the bullet does not name. Does not address the pair correlation function, or the conjecture's statement. Secondary coverage ties the method to Montgomery's 1973 pair-correlation approach; the post itself says it draws on prior research by mathematicians and does not, in the text I read, name the pair correlation conjecture.
events.remains: The pair correlation conjecture entirely; the RH itself; the simplicity of zeros is in the companion paper (see alpoge-furman-2026) and not in this claim.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman, 'More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line', arXiv 2608.13637 (v1 13 Aug 2026; v2 19 Aug 2026). The abstract says 'We prove unconditionally that at least two thirds of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function' are simple and on the critical line, counted with multiplicity, and at least five sixths are distinct; it reports improved constants (0.6725 and 0.8362 with a Montgomery–Taylor window) over prior records of 5/12 and 0.6603. The method 'replaces the Riemann Hypothesis assumption in Montgomery's 1973 deduction with a rank-trace inequality applied to a finite compression of Weil's Hermitian form'. It extends to primitive Dirichlet L-functions and is 'stated to be formally verified in Lean 4'. The arXiv comments field says: 'Proof discovered autonomously by Claude (Anthropic); verified and communicated by the listed authors.' The abstract does not mention the pair correlation conjecture, and does not claim a result on it. The Anthropic post does not link this arXiv record; I take it to be the 'Claude's paper' the post describes, from matching content and dates, not from a link.
events.revisions: v1 13 Aug 2026; v2 19 Aug 2026 (per arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Unconditionally: at least 2/3 of the zeros simple and on the critical line; at least 5/6 distinct; extended to primitive Dirichlet L-functions. Scope: proportions of simple and critical-line zeros, not the pair correlation function. Montgomery's 1973 deduction is the starting point, with RH replaced.
events.remains: The pair correlation conjecture as stated, including its normalised pair correlation function.
events.doubts: Both authors are Anthropic mathematicians, and the comments field credits the discovery to Claude, so the independence of the verification is limited. No external expert verdict is published on the arXiv record. The later Lamzouri preprint (2609.02882) engages with it and says the argument is 'technically intricate'. The Lean sorry-status was not checked. The PDF was not read; the main theorem comes from the abstract.
events.direction: Cuts for the simplicity and critical-line question, not the bullet's quantity: it proves an unconditional 2/3 proportion result.

The Lean formalisation is not attributed to Claude on this page; the Anthropic post says Claude produced a formally verifiable proof.

events.what_happened: Youness Lamzouri, 'A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line', arXiv 2609.02882 (v1 2 Sep 2026; v2 8 Sep 2026; 17 pages; math.NT and math.CV). The abstract says it is an 'unconditional proof' that 'more than 67.25% of the non-trivial zeros' are simple and on the critical line, that 'at least 83.62%' are distinct, that the proportion that are simple or critical (or both) is at least 88.76%, and that the average of the simple and critical proportions is at least 83.62%. It says the argument was 'produced by an internal research version of Claude developed by Anthropic' and that 'The argument produced by Claude is technically intricate'. It says its 'two additional estimates are neither stated nor proved in the Claude paper', and that the bounds were 'verified by two mathematicians at Anthropic, Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman'. The abstract does not mention the pair correlation conjecture. No journal reference, no Lean mention, and no affiliation are listed on the abstract page. The PDF text was not extractable with my tools.

events.delivers: Unconditionally: more than 67.25% of the non-trivial zeros are simple and on the critical line; at least 83.62% distinct. Scope: proportions of simple and critical-line zeros, not the pair correlation function. It adds two estimates not in the Claude paper.

disputes.summary: Two claims of a proof of the conjecture have different scope and hypotheses: Jerby (arXiv 2511.18275, Nov 2025) proves it for Hardy's Z-function assuming RH; Tishkov (preprints.ru, 29 June 2026) claims an unconditional proof for ζ(s). Neither has been engaged by a referee or expert in my searches, and they do not contradict each other because they differ in hypothesis.

The arXiv comments field for 2608.13637 says the proof was 'discovered autonomously by Claude', while the Anthropic post describes the human role as studying and validating the work. Secondary coverage, not checked against the post, says the humans' role was mainly to encourage the model. Lamzouri's abstract attributes the argument to Claude and says it was verified by the same two Anthropic mathematicians.
One secondary outlet gives 5 October 2026 as the date of the Anthropic announcement; the post itself is dated 10 August 2026 and was updated 13 August 2026. I used the post's own date.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 the conjecture itself appears to remain unproven in the literature I could find. The Wikipedia article (last edited 5 Oct 2026 per the fetched text) presents it as a conjecture with strong numerical support and no proof, and says Goldston, Lee, Schettler and Suriajaya's RH-free reformulation is 'not yet peer reviewed'. Two preprints claim proofs of the conjecture as stated, and neither has public expert engagement that I could find. Jerby (arXiv 2511.18275, v1 23 Nov 2025, v2 19 Dec 2025) claims the GUE pair-correlation law for the zeros of Hardy's Z-function under RH. Under RH those are the ordinates of ζ's non-trivial zeros, so the scope matches the bullet, but the assumption is RH, which Montgomery also assumed. I read the abstract, Theorem C and the first 100,000 characters of the HTML, but could not reach Section 9 where the proof sits, so the argument is unchecked. Tishkov (preprints.ru, 'Spectral Proof of the Montgomery Pair Correlation Conjecture via the Operator H_{X,N} and Free Probability Theory', 29 June 2026) claims an unconditional proof for ζ's zeros. The platform's notice says it is an unreviewed preprint, and its PDF could not be extracted with my tools, so the argument is unchecked. The author's reference list includes two of his own unreviewed preprints, and a search snippet (not opened) shows an earlier Zenodo claim of a proof of RH by the same author. Both claims are close calls for the judging pass: the scope matches the bullet, but there is no referee, no verification, and the load-bearing steps (Section 9 for Jerby; the H_{X,N} limit and explicit-formula link for Tishkov) are unread by me. Most of the window's other activity is conditional or analogue. Goldston, Lee, Schettler and Suriajaya (arXiv 2503.15449, 19 Mar 2025; 2507.06823, 9 Jul 2025) derive simplicity and critical-line consequences from the conjecture without RH, and treat an Alternative-Hypothesis variant. Baluyot, Goldston, Suriajaya and Turnage-Butterbaugh (2501.14545, 24 Jan 2025) work under a narrow-box hypothesis, and Goldston and Suriajaya (2511.20059, 25 Nov 2025) under a conditional RH removal. Banks (2502.20569, 27 Feb 2025) studies sums of two ordinates under RH and withdrew v1 theorems that had gaps. The unconditional restricted-range theorem (Baluyot et al., arXiv 2306.04799, 7 June 2023, Acta Arith. 214 (2024)) predates the window. Kandhil, Languasco and Moree (2607.14515, 16 Jul 2026) apply pair-correlation hypotheses for Dirichlet L-functions to two different problems. The AI-credited events of August and September 2026 concern a different quantity from the one the bullet names. Anthropic's post (10 Aug 2026, updated 13 Aug) reports an unreleased research version of Claude raising the proven proportion of zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, using 31 million output tokens over two Claude Code sessions, with a Lean formalisation. arXiv 2608.13637 (Alpöge and Furman, 13 Aug 2026) proves unconditionally that at least two thirds of zeros are simple and on the critical line, and its comments field credits the discovery to Claude. Lamzouri (arXiv 2609.02882, 2 Sep 2026) gives an unconditional extension to 67.25% and says the argument was 'produced by an internal research version of Claude developed by Anthropic'. None of these three names the pair correlation function as its object, and the Anthropic post does not mention the conjecture in the text I read. Secondary coverage ties the method to Montgomery's 1973 pair-correlation approach, but I did not verify that in the lab's own text. AI searches for the conjecture itself (AlphaEvolve, Gemini, GPT, Lean formalisations, Erdős-problem trackers, the 2026 Connes survey) found no system credited with the pair correlation conjecture. The Forrester–Wei note (2601.13488), which one search snippet described as stating the conjecture is open in general, does not mention the conjecture; that snippet attribution was wrong.
competing_reading: Read Jerby (RH-conditional, Z-function zeros) and Tishkov (unconditional, ζ zeros) as the first complete proofs of the conjecture on the bullet's own scope, so that the bullet would be settled, conditionally on RH in one case and unconditionally in the other, pending checks. On this reading the Claude-credited work counts as AI contribution to the problem's proof technology, because its route runs through Montgomery's pair-correlation method and the Alpöge–Furman argument is stated to rest on it. The opposite reading is that neither preprint is a credible resolution: both are unrefereed, Jerby's proof is loosely specified in the parts I could read and its key section is unread by me, and Tishkov's author has other unreviewed claims. On that reading the bullet is untouched, and the Claude-credited results change only the proportion of zeros that are simple or on the line.
what_would_settle_it: For the two proof claims: a referee report or journal acceptance; or a written expert verification of Jerby's Theorem C and proof (Section 9 and the DBM universality input) and of Tishkov's H_{X,N} semicircle and GUE-statistics claims and his explicit-formula link; a numerical test of the H_{X,N} claim; or a Lean formalisation of either, checked for sorry. For the AI question: the full text and contribution statement of arXiv 2608.13637 and of the Anthropic paper (the post's changelog says it was updated on 13 Aug), a statement from Alpöge, Furman, Conrey or Goldston on whether any Claude-credited argument touches the normalised pair correlation of ζ zeros, and a check of the Lean repositories for sorry. For the scope question: a statement from Goldston or Lamzouri on whether the Claude argument uses pair correlation for ζ zeros as an input, or only the Montgomery 1973 deduction under RH.
